### Proof

Weakly-increasing superdiagonal partitions with k parts are in bijection with reverse 1-compositions with k parts. Indeed, given a weakly-increasing superdiagonal partition, removing \(i-1\) from the ith part for each \(1\le i\le k\) results in a reverse 1-composition.

Let F(q, u, y) be the generating function for non-empty 1-compositions where q marks the size of the composition, u marks the size of the last part, and y marks the number of parts.

To find a functional equation for F(q, u, y), we use the adding-a-slice method (see [12]), that produces 1-compositions by appending one part at a time. The first term below corresponds to the case of a composition with one part, the second term describes the addition of a part to a non-empty composition, and the third term subtracts off the case where the new part increases by two or more.

$$\begin{aligned} F(q,u,y)&= \frac{quy}{1-qu} + \frac{quy}{1-qu} F(q,1,y) - \frac{q^2u^2y}{1-qu} F(q,qu,y). \end{aligned}$$

Replacing \(y^k\) by \(t^kq^{\left( {\begin{array}{c}k\\ 2\end{array}}\right) }\) in Eq. (6) for all \(k\ge 1\), we obtain

$$\begin{aligned} A(q,t)= \sum _{k\ge 1}t^kq^{\left( {\begin{array}{c}k\\ 2\end{array}}\right) }[y^k]\sum _{i\ge 0}\left( \sum _{j \ge 1} a(j)y^j\right) ^i. \end{aligned}$$

We can also express the coefficient of \(y^k\) in Eq. (6) as a sum over weakly-increasing partitions \(\pi =(\pi _1^{i_1},\pi _2^{i_2},\dots ,\pi _s^{i_s})\) of k:

$$\begin{aligned} A(q,t)=\sum _{k\ge 1}t^kq^{\left( {\begin{array}{c}k\\ 2\end{array}}\right) }\sum _{\text {partitions } \pi \text { of } k}\left( {\begin{array}{c}i_1+i_2+\dots +i_s\\ i_1,i_2,\dots ,i_s\end{array}}\right) (a(\pi _1))^{i_1}(a(\pi _2))^{i_2}\dots (a(\pi _s))^{i_s}. \end{aligned}$$

\(\square \)

$$\begin{aligned} A(q,t)=\sum _{k\ge 1}t^kq^{\left( {\begin{array}{c}k\\ 2\end{array}}\right) }\sum _{\text {compositions } (c_1,c_2,\dots ,c_i) \text { of } k}a(c_1)a(c_2)\dots a(c_i) \end{aligned}$$

Let α be a composition and β be a weak composition. A row-strict reverse shin-tableau (RSRST) of
shape α and type β is a filling of the diagram of α with positive integers such that the entries in each
row are strictly decreasing from left to right and the entries in each column are weakly increasing
from top to bottom where each integer i appears βi times. These are essentially a row-strict version
of the reverse shin-tableaux. A row-strict reverse shin-tableau of shape α |= n is standard (SRSRST)
if it includes the entries 1 through n each exactly once.

OFFSET

0,6

COMMENTS

Every sequence can be uniquely split into a sequence of non-overlapping runs. For example, the runs of (2,2,1,1,1,3,2,2) are ((2,2),(1,1,1),(3),(2,2)), with sums (4,3,3,4).

The k-th composition in standard order (graded reverse-lexicographic, A066099) is obtained by taking the set of positions of 1's in the reversed binary expansion of k, prepending 0, taking first differences, and reversing again. This gives a bijective correspondence between nonnegative integers and integer compositions.
